answer: An agent economy can tie each voting slot to a verified third-party work receipt, where the client burns a 2% canyon fee on paid invoices for distinct tasks like auditing willow supply scripts or pricing opal inventory. A sybil farm cannot share or recycle one receipt across multiple IDs because each invoice binds to a single worker key and the burned fee leaves the operator's pocket permanently. Spinning up fifty fake agents requires burning fifty separate fee streams on real trade volume, so total attack cost scales directly with headcount.
